messages:
Sam Nguyen: Quick q — I'm planning to move to Puerto Rico (PR) with an intended move date of 2026-07-01. How does that affect WFH stipend eligibility, payroll withholding, and benefits enrollment? Also curious whether Redwood offers any relocation reimbursement for this kind of move. cc @Jamal (People Ops)

Jamal (People Ops): Congrats, Sam! A few things to flag: relocation reimbursements are handled case-by-case (manager + People Ops sign-off). We typically offer a one-time reimbursement for major inter-island / interstate moves when approved. For the WFH stipend — yes, it's prorated based on the active payroll address on file for the month.

Elya (Payroll): Heads-up: Puerto Rico has different payroll/tax rules than the states. We'll need notice to change your payroll jurisdiction. Please submit the Change of Residence form and your new address ASAP. We usually need ~30 days to avoid retroactive withholding adjustments. Also DM me the SSN and the move effective date so payroll can estimate any split-pay impacts.

Olivia (Legal): From a legal perspective PR can create a tax/employer nexus depending on business activities there. For an individual move we usually do a quick nexus check; if the company needs to register there it could add steps. Jamal, can you kick off a nexus review once Sam files the intake? Sam, include what parts of your role will remain US-remote vs any PR-based product/ops work.

Devon (Manager): Happy to support. Sam, please drop a short cost estimate and any contractor quotes you have. I can approve up to our manager-level threshold and then loop in Jamal for People Ops sign-off.

hr-bot: New ticket created — HR-5821 (relocation + payroll review). Link: https://redwood.internal/desk/HR-5821

Sam Nguyen: Filed the Change of Residence form here: https://redwood.internal/notion/forms/change-of-residence and uploaded a move estimate (~$2,200). My role stays the same remotely; no planned customer-facing travel from PR.

Jamal (People Ops): Got it, thanks. We'll triage HR-5821 and route to Payroll + Legal. Expect an initial response in 3–5 business days. Regarding the WFH stipend: if payroll jurisdiction changes mid-month, stipend is prorated for that month based on the active payroll address on the payroll run date — we'll confirm exact proration math when payroll triages.

Elya (Payroll): One more practical note: moving to PR can cause a split pay period if the move happens mid-pay-period; that sometimes requires a manual reconciliation line on the next paycheck. We'll flag that in HR-5821 so Finance can prepare. DM'd you a secure upload link for SSN and ID.

Sam Nguyen: Sent the docs via the secure link. Appreciate the quick responses — will wait for the HR-5821 update. :pray:

Jamal (People Ops): Thanks, team. We'll keep the ticket updated and post the official decision here once Legal finishes the nexus check. If anyone needs additional docs from Sam, I'll ping. :thumbsup:
